narrative:
The machine learning model predicted a 53% chance that you would fail the bar exam, which is a significant concern for your application to law school. This probability indicates that, based on the data from previous students, there is a greater than even likelihood that you would not pass the exam on your first attempt.

Your application was denied primarily due to three key factors that influenced this prediction. First, your decision to work part-time while studying was a notable concern. Most successful applicants tend to work full-time, which suggests that balancing work and study may impact your preparation for the bar exam. 

Next, your performance in your first year of studies placed you in a higher decile compared to many accepted students, indicating strong initial academic achievement. However, your third-year performance was slightly below the average of accepted students, which may raise questions about your consistency and readiness for the challenges of the bar exam.

Lastly, your LSAT score was below the average of those who were accepted, which is a critical indicator of your potential success in law school and on the bar exam. While your undergraduate GPA is respectable, it still falls short of the average for accepted students.

To improve your chances in the future, consider focusing on enhancing your academic performance, particularly in your final year, and possibly reevaluating your work commitments to allow for more dedicated study time. Additionally, preparing for and retaking the LSAT could strengthen your application.
